what_happened: The job was asked to speed up the slowest test binary using timings from the newest green main CI run. The verifier rejected it: 3 of 5 acceptance criteria were unmet, with 3 blocker or major findings. The unmet criteria were: the CHANGELOG entry listing ten binaries slowest first with their "finished in" seconds and the run id; the CHANGELOG statement of before and after local time for the slowest binary (or a statement that it cannot be fixed without losing coverage); and a run of only the changed binary that passes faster than the stated "before" time. The findings say no CI timings were read, no ten-slowest list was written and no binary was sped up. The CHANGELOG entry recorded a job failure instead of a project change, and the evidence for criterion 5 did not cite commands that ran. No failed check is named. The producer apparently could not get the CI timings, wrote a failure note into the CHANGELOG, and stopped.
cause: The request's first step depends on data from outside the repo (GitHub CI run timings for the newest green main run). The isolated producer likely has no network or gh access, and nothing checks reachability or supplies the data before dispatch. The acceptance criteria also made the CHANGELOG entry mandatory even when no data could be fetched. Because there was no way to stop early with a clear "blocked" outcome, the producer wrote a failure note into a project file, and only the final verifier found that no work was done.
prevention: Before dispatch, resolve each external data source a request names (CI run timings, logs, GitHub) and either fetch it in the orchestrator and put it in the producer's input as a file (for example a generated timings file with the run id), or hold the job as blocked with a stated reason when it cannot be reached. The producer should also have a defined "blocked" report, so it ends without writing failure notes into the CHANGELOG or other project files.
proposed_request: Speed up the slowest athena test binary using timings from the newest green main CI run. Athena fetches the timings before the producer starts. It finds the newest green main run id, extracts each test binary's "finished in" seconds, and writes them to a read-only input file in the producer's working copy. If it cannot fetch them, it holds the job as blocked with the reason and the producer does not run. Then do this. (1) Add a CHANGELOG.md entry listing the ten slowest test binaries, slowest first, each with its seconds, and naming the run id. (2) Find the cause of the slowest binary's time and fix it without removing or weakening any test. State its local time before and after, each measured by running only that binary (cargo test -p <package> --test <name>). If the cause cannot be fixed without losing coverage, say so and change no code. (3) Show that the changed binary passes and its "finished in" time is below the "before" time. The evidence must cite the commands that actually ran. Do not write failure notes into CHANGELOG.md; the entry describes only a change to the project.
